Use the grammar and structures listed, actively and accurately, assuming GCSE grammar is known.
Use articles: singular and plural, and diminutives.
Use nouns: gender, singular and plural forms, agreement, direct and oblique forms.
Use pronouns: declension; personal, demonstrative, possessive, numeral, reflexive, interrogative; polite and familiar.
Use adjectives: gender, agreement, declension, comparative, superlative, demonstrative, interrogative, possessive.
Use adverbs: comparison and interrogative.
Use infinitives, present, past and future tenses, imperfective and perfective aspects, and forms of address.
Use main verbs in non-causative and causative forms, auxiliary verbs, passive with 'jaanda hai' and 'chaahida'.
Use copula forms, personal forms (subjunctive, imperative) and non-personal forms (imperfective, perfective, potential, conjunctive participle, future subjunctive).
Use prepositions such as from, below, on, with.
Use conjunctions, particles, subordinators, and separable and inseparable possession constructions.
Use cardinal, ordinal, indefinite and collective numbers and fractions.
Use expressions of quantity and time.
Vary word order flexibly for semantic emphasis.
Study a set literary text and film, or two texts, and respond critically in writing in Panjabi.
Choose either one text and one film or two texts from the lists.
Study one or two of the set texts: Noori, Ristian de Rang, Savee Pattar.
Study one of the set films: Asa Nu Maan Watna Da (2004), Jatt and Juliet 2 (2013).
Choose a research topic, cover all its bullet points, select Panjabi information from varied sources including the internet and summarise findings in an essay.
Research the role of women: changing role, role in the family, impact of working women.
Research social issues: crime and consequences, impact of poverty, solutions.
Research tourism: tourist infrastructure, popular sites, regional food.
Research the 1947 Partition: background, events, impact on modern society.
